notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1787). Words follow the Schirmer vocal score's spelling and punctuation, and its repeats of words and lines. Where the print differs from the libretto the words follow the print: Zerlina "ajuto", "Scelerato!" (libretto scellerato; sung with ll), her second "soccoretemi" printed with one r (sung soccorretemi), "son morta" without the libretto's "o", and "sà," with an accent in bars 115 and 117; "Ah gittiamo giù la porta" (libretto gettiamo); Don Giovanni "Ecco il birbo chi t'ha offesa" (libretto che); Donna Elvira "malvaggio" (libretto malvagio; sung malvagio); Donna Anna "poss' io" printed as two words. Don Giovanni's "(Meco tu dei ballare; Zerlina, vien pur quà!)" in bars 3-8 is printed in small notes with a footnote (not in the autograph score, found in the earliest copied voice parts) and is not in the libretto; it is sung here as part of his line. The first bar also ends the previous piece ("Riposate, vezzose ragazze!"): Don Giovanni's "-rini!" on its downbeat is the end of "ballerini" and is left out of this piece's words. IPA, word meanings and translations were drafted for this app (S31) and the IPA was checked against Castel. IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ. Translation literal, for meaning.
